Notation of dmai

Source: R/common-notation.R
dmai_notation.Rd

The symbols used in the help pages and vignettes of dmai, with their meaning and the argument or result component that holds them. The notation follows one rule throughout: scalars are upper-case letters in normal face (\(P\), \(R\)), indices lower-case italic (\(i, j\)), vectors lower-case bold (\(\mathbf{y}\), \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\)) and matrices upper-case bold (\(\mathbf{X}\), \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\)).

Usage

dmai_notation(format = c("table", "path", "tex"))

Arguments

format

"table" (default: a data.table with columns symbol (LaTeX), text (plain text), kind (scalar, index, vector, matrix, set, function, operator), meaning and argument), "path" (the path of notation.csv) or "tex" (the path of Notations.tex, the notation appendix used in the articles).

Value

See format.

See also

Other dmai utilities: dmai_reference(), dmai_save(), dmai_theme()

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

dmai_notation(
    format = c("table", "path", "tex")[1]
  )
#>                   symbol    text     kind
#>                   <char>  <char>   <char>
#>  1:                    n       n   scalar
#>  2:                    T       T   scalar
#>  3:                 i, j     i j    index
#>  4:                    t       t    index
#>  5:               x_{it}    x_it   scalar
#>  6:               r_{it}    r_it   scalar
#>  7:                  R_t     R_t   scalar
#>  8:            \\pi_{it}   pi_it   scalar
#>  9:               s_{it}    s_it   scalar
#> 10:        \\bar{s}_{it} sbar_it   scalar
#> 11:        \\mathbf{x}_t     x_t   vector
#> 12: \\boldsymbol{\\pi}_t    pi_t   vector
#> 13:        \\mathbf{s}_t     s_t   vector
#> 14:          \\mathbf{X}       X   matrix
#> 15:                  Q_t     Q_t   scalar
#> 16:                  V_t     V_t   scalar
#> 17:                  E_t     E_t   scalar
#> 18:                  P_t     P_t   scalar
#> 19:            \\kappa_t kappa_t   scalar
